system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: injects the patient profile and current datetime as structured context
system_prompt_style.note: User agent prompt uses format_prompt_safe with scenario/profile variables; assistant prompt similarly templated.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: the agent receives the full conversation history and the patient profile
env_context_strategy.note: Closest value: the environment context (structured patient record) is injected up front rather than a directory listing; no repo/file tree exists. Agent can also query sandbox tools.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: On each turn, the agent receives the full conversation history and the patient profile
context_compaction.note: No condenser/truncation described; conversations capped at 15 turns.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Every turn is captured in a structured conversation trace (messages, tool calls, and tool results).

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: The assistant is implemented as a ReAct [Yao et al., 2023] (Reasoning and Acting) agent built using LangGraph
tool_call_format.note: LangGraph ReAct agent uses provider tool-calling APIs (ChatBedrockConverse/ChatOpenAI/ChatAnthropic).

tool_count.evidence_quote: providing 15 tools within a stateful sandbox across four categories (appointments, prescriptions, telehealth, and profile management)

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Appointments (5) — list_doctors, get_available_appointments, schedule_appointment, cancel_appointment, list_appointments
edit_primitive.note: No file-editing tool; sandbox tools only.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: Each tool ships with a structured natural-language specification of its purpose, required and optional parameters, return format, and behavioral preconditions

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: stateful tools across four categories: appointments, prescriptions, telehealth, and profile management
protocol_standardization.note: No MCP/A2A mentioned anywhere in README or paper.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: the assistant is a LangGraph ReAct agent that reasons and acts against the healthcare sandbox

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: the prompt does not include few-shot examples, chain-of-thought scaffolding, or model-specific optimizations
planning_granularity.note: Guidelines section gives a behavioral recipe; no stored plan object.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: The conversation loop is a dual-agent exchange: the assistant is a LangGraph ReAct agent
multi_agent_topology.note: The system under evaluation is a single agent; the simulated patient is the benchmark's user, not a collaborating agent.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: the agent receives the full conversation history and the patient profile, reasons about the appropriate next action, and may invoke one or more sandbox tools before producing its response

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: The user agent is a plain LLM conditioned on the scenario, clinically grounded profile, and a personality type
human_in_loop.note: Human role is simulated by an LLM; no human approval gate in the loop.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: On each turn, the agent receives the full conversation history and the patient profile
short_term_state.note: Sandbox holds mutable environment state, but the agent's own working state is the message list.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: The sandbox is generated at the start of each conversation using LLM and persists for the duration of that conversation.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: Pre-initializes conversations.json with null slots, skips entries that already have results, and writes each result to its slot as soon as it completes.
state_persistence.note: Resume is at case granularity (`--run-dir` skips completed conversations), not mid-conversation.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Each conversation is scored by an LLM-as-a-Jury against a reusable suite of over a hundred clinician-grounded, conversation-agnostic criteria

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Conversations that encounter unrecoverable agent errors are terminated with an error marker and excluded from aggregate scoring.
retry_policy.note: LLM API transport retries exist (retry_sync_with_backoff) but no task-level retry.

rollback.evidence_quote: the shared mutable data store that all tools read from and write to during the conversation
rollback.note: No undo/rollback of sandbox mutations; sandbox is regenerated per conversation.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: steps 2–3 repeat for up to 15 turns. Conversations terminate early when the user agent decides its request is resolved
termination_condition.note: Turn cap configurable via max_turns (default_config shows "max_turns": 10); termination signal emitted by the simulated patient.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: For a model not in the registry, provide a custom spec with model_id and max_tokens
cost_controls.note: max_tokens is a per-response cap, not a run budget; no cost cap or caching described.

timeouts.evidence_quote: steps 2–3 repeat for up to 15 turns
timeouts.note: Only turn caps, which are not timeouts; no timeout configuration surfaced in the available evidence.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: The sandbox is generated at the start of each conversation using LLM and persists for the duration of that conversation.
execution_isolation.note: Tools mutate an in-process Python data store; no subprocess/container execution.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: the shared mutable data store that all tools read from and write to during the conversation
filesystem_access.note: Closest value: agent touches only the in-memory simulated healthcare state, not a real filesystem.

network_policy.evidence_quote: Each conversation operates within an isolated, dynamically generated healthcare sandbox
network_policy.note: Agent actions have no network egress; only the harness itself calls model APIs.

permission_model.evidence_quote: may invoke one or more sandbox tools before producing its response
permission_model.note: Tool-level preconditions exist inside tools, but no authorisation layer over model-emitted calls.

tracing.evidence_quote: Every turn is captured in a structured conversation trace (messages, tool calls, and tool results).

replayability.evidence_quote: Resume into an existing run directory (skips completed experiments)
replayability.note: Saved conversations can be re-evaluated (`evaluate --run-dir`), but model outputs are not replayed deterministically.

eval_hooks.note: The repo is itself the benchmark harness with a built-in evaluation runner.

guardrails.evidence_quote: the framework strips internal reasoning blocks before passing the response to the user agent
guardrails.note: Closest available control: output filtering of thinking blocks; safety rules are prompt-level only. Arguably output_filters — flagged as ambiguous.

target_domain.evidence_quote: PatientAgentBench benchmarks patient-facing agentic healthcare; it evaluates a foundation model, wrapped in an agent with a sandbox of healthcare tools
target_domain.note: Domain is patient-facing healthcare workflows; not covered by existing values.

open_source.note: Full source released but CC-BY-NC is not an OSI licence (non-commercial).

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: PatientAgentBench supports three model access channels, and any role (assistant, simulated patient, evaluator, sandbox, seed generator, analyzer) can use any of them

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: This repository hosts the reference implementation for the paper

first_release_date.note: No tags in evidence; basis is pinned commit date 2026-07-29 / paper v1 date.

pinned_version.note: No tagged release available; pinned to main.
